# The U.S. Supreme Court: A Bass-Fishing Tournament Breakdown

## The Anglers Themselves

The nine Justices are your **tournament pros**—the ones who've qualified for the Bassmaster Classic of jurisprudence. You don't just show up to this tournament; you get invited by the League Commissioner (the President) and then you have to survive the **weigh-in interrogation** by the Tournament Committee (the Senate), who poke your livewell and ask if your bass are legally caught.

Once you're in, you're in for life—or until you decide to hang up your rod and retire to a quiet pond somewhere.

## The Cases as Fish

Thousands of lawyers cast their lines every year hoping to hook the Court's attention. This is the **petition for certiorari**, or as we call it in the tournament, "getting your bait noticed." Most of these lures get ignored entirely. The Justices only bite on about 70 cases a year—they're trophy hunters, see. They're not interested in your dinky little crappie disputes. They want the **lunkers**, the constitutional largemouths that'll shake up the whole lake ecosystem.
